P1 — `NAMED.md:1563` / `scripts/m360_orphans.py:245-251` — The first VERIFIED row claims per-widget builder/REBUILD counts (`8/12/14/8/13/4/7` and `…/11/14/4/7`), but no gate reads those counts. `G1a` only checks that there are 7 common widget offsets; `G2a` only checks total rows = 66 and distinct ids; `G2b` only checks total queries = 70. The printed per-widget tables are evidence, not gated facts. This matters because the milestone’s central “seven widgets, not a seventh page” measurement can be wrong per widget while all cited gates stay green.

P1 — `NAMED.md:1563` — The row names `MU1,MU3,MU19`, but none of those mutants reddens `G2b`, the only gate for “REBUILD queries 70”. The actual mutant for that claim is `MU4` (`scripts/m360_mutate.py:31-32`), which is not named in any VERIFIED row. Under the repo rule, every VERIFIED claim row must name the mutant that reddens it; this row violates that for the REBUILD-70 half of the claim.

P1 — `NAMED.md:1565` / `scripts/m360_orphans.py:318-331` — The miss-semantics row claims the set-by-id path also scans from 0 and shifts by the scanned index, but the named mutants are only `MU8,MU9,MU21`. `MU8`/`MU9` attack `G3a` (`is_checked`), and `MU21` attacks the `jge` bound in `G3c`; none attacks `G3b`, the gate for `set_checked`/`0x6050d4`. The actual mutant for `G3b` is `MU10` (`scripts/m360_mutate.py:43-45`), omitted from the claim row. So the “shift `<node+0x14>`” part of the claim is not backed by a named mutant.

P1 — `NAMED.md:1567` / `scripts/m360_orphans.py:373-381` — The claim says `0x37/0x38/0x39` are radio handlers of classes `1/2/3`, but no gate asserts the class bytes. `G4a` only asserts the decoded handler kind is `"radio"` and the relabel controls are `0x4e/0x4c/0x4d`; `G4b` asserts masks/source; `G4c` asserts no `set_checked` call. The class numbers come from `byte(0x4938E0 + (x - 0x13))` at `scripts/m360_orphans.py:365-367`, but that value is printed, not gated. A wrong class-byte table interpretation could still pass all cited gates.

P1 — `NAMED.md:1568` / `scripts/m360_orphans.py:430-433` — The claim says absent-id writes are “only `(0x913c,0x50)`”, but `G5b` does not assert uniqueness. It only checks that no bad pair is in `0x7aec` or `0x8614` and that `(0x913c,0x50)` is present. Extra absent-id writes in other widgets would not redden the gate. The word “only” is therefore not verified.

P1 — `NAMED.md:1568` / `scripts/m360_orphans.py:407-427` — “A/V+0x8614 bits unwritten” is not fully gated. `bad_pairs` is built only from paint jump-table entries and only checks whether the first reachable call is `SET_ID`. It does not census all `set_checked` callers outside the paint window, nor does it trace `toggle-by-bit` indices or `add_item` bit indices. The instrument prints “callers of set-by-id: 24 (9 in paint, 15 elsewhere)” at `scripts/m360_orphans.py:399-402`, but the 15 non-paint callers are never checked for absent-id writes. Thus “never written” is broader than the gate.

P2 — `NAMED.md:1567` — The evidence citation for the radio-handler row is only `:86`, which is `G4a`. The claim also includes masks/source bits (`a4c:11/10`, `a50:14`) and no-set-by-id behavior, which are gated by `G4b` and `G4c` at evidence lines `:87` and `:88`. The citation should include those lines or the row should be split. As written, the cited line does not read the full claim.

P2 — `SESSION_NOTES.md:727` / `evidence/m360_orphans.txt:126-127` — The session notes cite the digest at `evidence/m360_orphans.txt:126`, but line 126 is the final gate line `[PASS] M360: 22/22 gates`; the digest is line 127. The digest is computed and printed by the instrument (`scripts/m360_orphans.py:605-606`), so the artifact is fine, but the evidence pointer is off by one.

P2 — `scripts/m360_orphans.py:383-390` — `G4c` checks “no radio handler calls `0x6050d4`” by scanning a fixed 60-instruction window from `htab[1]`, `htab[2]`, `htab[3]`, not from the actual handlers decoded for ids `0x37/0x38/0x39`. If the class-byte mapping changed but the handlers still decoded as radio with the expected controls, `G4c` could inspect the wrong handlers. It also uses a fixed window rather than the handler body boundary used by `handler_kind()` at `scripts/m360_orphans.py:337-343`, so it can miss a later `call` or include a neighboring handler’s `call`.

P2 — `scripts/m360_orphans.py:392-397` — The “stale `a48 & 0x1000`” claim is only weakly gated. `G4d` checks that the seventh block contains no textual `0xa48` reference and that the previous block’s last decoded mask is `0x1000`; it does not verify that `[ebp-0x8]` is actually loaded from that previous masked value, nor that the seventh block’s test operand is `[ebp-0x8]`. The test operand line is hardcoded at `scripts/m360_orphans.py:396-397`. The conclusion “all four states are 0” depends on dataflow facts that the gate does not read.
